title: Path of the Shaman — Warcraft III DE Performance Audit and Optimization Plan

repository.name: wc3-path-of-the-shaman
repository.source_of_truth: Actual dev checkout and active game installation, rather than historical documentation, main-branch search results, or assistant assumptions
repository.jass_api_baseline: Warcraft III 3.0.0 / build 24268 according to AGENTS.md; verify against installed game files and current build before implementing

mission.primary: Analyze whether PotS can obtain meaningful FPS/frame-time gains in Warcraft III DE graphics through already-available natives, script optimizations, smarter visibility management and asset/renderer changes; produce a benchmarkable, risk-ranked implementation roadmap.
mission.secondary: Identify improvements to existing systems without losing gameplay, saved-state, visual or multiplayer compatibility.
desired_outputs: Detailed code-evidenced analysis of current performance systems and all actionable native API opportunities
Prioritized optimization backlog with per-file implementation designs (no edits yet)
Proposed isolated benchmarks and acceptance criteria
Confirmed non-opportunities and reasons to avoid them

critical_rules: Do not edit or commit existing source code, object data, imports, World Editor content, libraries or configuration in this audit phase.
Do not replace proven existing systems wholesale. Prefer small compatible changes preserving public APIs, behavior, initialized data and active dependencies.
Read AGENTS.md and all relevant local guidelines before interpreting files. Historical analysis reports are clues, not proof of current defects.

Verify every proposed native's exact spelling, signature, availability and semantics in active _Blizzard/common.j and relevant _Blizzard/Blizzard.j wrappers; cross-check with game installation/PTR only when relevant.
Distinguish confirmed source facts, untested hypotheses, measured results and unknowns explicitly; never fabricate measurements or assert FPS gains based only on algorithmic complexity.

Preserve SD and DE modes, cutscenes, special cameras, camera locality, map transitions, gameplay AI/combat/quests, pathing, interactive doodads/destructables, persistent units, saved state and normal multiplayer synchronization.

Do not create, destroy, hide or modify synced game objects inside a GetLocalPlayer guard without proof that the operation is local-safe. Camera and UI operations may be local; simulation state normally is not.
Visual hiding is not proof of reduced AI, physics, pathfinding, animation or trigger processing. Identify which costs a proposed change actually affects.
ShowUnit and ShowDestructable can have gameplay and trigger interactions: test visibility, pathing, selection, interactions, resurrection and ownership carefully.
Do not assume setting effect alpha to zero or frame visibility false removes simulation or draw-call cost; benchmark.
Do not confuse reducing native call count with reducing GPU rendering cost.
Exclude deprecated, unknown or non-existent APIs. Do not invent renderer controls absent from common.j.
Maintain present NPC simulation and world continuity unless explicit alternative LOD policies are specified with testable gameplay semantics.
Keep JASS/vJASS and JassHelper compatibility; compile with the normal World Editor/JassHelper pipeline, not pjass alone.
Respect World Editor export boundaries in AGENTS.md: document WE-only follow-ups without changing exported map data or _MISC/war3map.wts.
Do not use strong benchmark claims from historic documents without rerunning measurements on the current dev build.

known_source_observations.observation: INTERVAL=0.2, DRAW_DISTANCE=5120, TILE_RESOLUTION=10 (512-unit tiles). ChangeTiles hides the previous (21x21) tile window and re-shows the new window, including overlap; native ShowDestructable calls can repeat unnecessarily.
known_source_observations.impact_model: With a one-cell horizontal move in interior terrain, up to 441 old + 441 new tile visits occur rather than 21 leaving + 21 entering; actual number of destructable toggles depends on content and state.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Differential tile-window updates reduce update spikes/camera-pan stutter.

known_source_observations.observation: Current implementation is v4.11.0; 64x64 hidden-unit grid, 0.10-second updates, 0.50-second visible sweeps, mostly event-driven discovery and full-map bootstrap rather than the obsolete UnitHider3 periodic world scans. Some recurring GroupAddGroup calls copy groups through a Blizzard.j wrapper.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Native fast group copying may reduce JASS overhead at hotspots; UnitHider4 is not an automatic rewrite candidate.

known_source_observations.observation: Angle interpolation increases FarZ toward full base distance at horizon angle >=345 degrees even for Heavy profile; baseline base FarZ is 10000 in CameraControl, and Medium at natural/default 304 degrees is approximately 6500 without zone cap.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: A profile-specific hard cap or jointly managed culling distances could reduce GPU workload at low camera pitches while preserving cinematics.

known_source_observations.observation: Camera control includes 0.03-second keyboard/drift loops, local middle-mouse orbit and per-player camera field updates; effective FarZ is applied locally. Camera mode/cinematic compatibility matters.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Reduce redundant camera field native calls and recalculate only on meaningful parameter changes if profiling finds the loop costly.

known_source_observations.observation: Rain impacts run every 0.15 seconds in active weather, recycle a ring of 16 special-effect slots through DestroyEffect/AddSpecialEffect and perform position, terrain and water checks. Weather also has existing FPS flags for ripple, clouds and steam suppression.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Profiling may justify reducing creation, terrain samples or effects; local camera effects require strict sync-safe handling.

known_source_observations.observation: UnitStats presently performs a ONE-TIME map scan and then event-driven updates. The older 2025 lag analysis incorrectly describes an ongoing 3-second whole-map scan as if still present.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Do not blindly apply the historical recommendation to disable or slow UnitStats.

known_source_observations.observation: GroupAddGroup(sourceGroup,destGroup) uses a ForGroup-based JASS wrapper, and may destroy source group via bj_wantDestroyGroup. GetUnitsInRectMatching and GetUnitsInRangeOfLocMatching allocate fresh groups and destroy passed filter expressions.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Fast natives and reusable groups/coordinate enumerations may improve hotspots if lifetime and argument semantics are preserved.

known_source_observations.observation: Active baseline declares BlzGroupAddGroupFast, BlzGroupRemoveGroupFast, BlzGetNumDoodads, BlzGetDoodadX/Y/Id, BlzSetSingleDoodadAnimation, SetDoodadAnimation/Rect, BlzSetSpecialEffectPosition, BlzFrameSetVisible, SetHDWaterParamsEx and BlzSetHDWaterReflectivity.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Several APIs enable more direct operations; they are not guaranteed to improve graphics performance merely by existing.

known_source_observations.path: DoodadRender (unknown path / potentially World Editor-embedded or external)
known_source_observations.observation: WeatherSystemV4 refers to DoodadRender, but the expected standalone library was not located in inspected dev paths.
known_source_observations.hypothesis: Search complete checkout, imports and World Editor sources before claiming any implementation or integration details.

known_source_observations.observation: Official Blizzard notice dated 2026-10-08 says live was reverted to 3.0.0 while 3.0.1 remained on PTR for more testing. Confirm latest installed build during audit.

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Build an immutable indexed doodad grid once; toggle presentation for only newly entered/exited visible tiles by doodad index instead of broad repeated searches
mandatory_verification: Test whether indexes start at 0 and the enumeration stable over load/save and gameplay
Test whether animation tokens 'show' and 'hide' behave on each relevant DE/SD doodad type
Benchmark a prototype against existing DoodadRender, and check near/far camera shifts, teleport and cinematic restore
Confirm doodad non-pathing behavior and effect on particles, lights and variation models

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Where appropriate replace JASS ForGroup-based GroupAddGroup copies in UnitHider4/other hot loops
mandatory_verification: Blizzard.j GroupAddGroup(source,destination) differs from native BlzGroupAddGroupFast(destination,source)
Check bj_wantDestroyGroup, group aliasing, membership, iteration stability, returned size and side effects
A/B test microbenchmark and real scenes; skip if negligible

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Replace clusters of separate X/Y/Z or yaw/pitch/roll updates for the same effect, where equivalent
mandatory_verification: Search actual project call sites
Preserve z terrain alignment and local camera semantics
Benchmark per-effect CPU time and visible artifacts
Avoid speculative changes to animated effects whose transform semantics differ

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Investigate show/hide animation behavior for scenery; do not confuse doodads and destructables
mandatory_verification: Verify show/hide on target game version and all model classes
Compare per-item and area-based work
Check whether hide actually reduces rendering costs and whether pathing and visibility restore work

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Replace repeated GetUnits... BJ allocation or unnecessary world scans with cached/reused groups and localized event-based tracking when safe
mandatory_verification: Do not impose counted-unit caps on combat/quest mechanics
Account for mutation during iteration
Free only owned groups/filters/locations

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Avoid redundant CameraControl/FarZ setter invocations and cache calculated fields only if this demonstrably affects CPU or stutter
mandatory_verification: Respect per-player local rendering
No changes to synchronized state behind GetLocalPlayer
Preserve smoothing, mouse orbit, cutscenes and scripted camera priority

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Audit expensive UI frame updates and strings generated while hidden; gate scripted work by actual panel state
mandatory_verification: Hiding frames is not equivalent to stopping their JASS update loop
Avoid breaking input focus, tooltips, inventory and custom UI

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Test whether limiting water visual complexity actually improves DE GPU timings
mandatory_verification: These are quality/state controls, not documented FPS toggles
Retain environmental appearance and water physics
Only pursue if A/B benchmark confirms gains

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Review effect lifecycle and actual renderer cost instead of blindly setting alpha to zero
mandatory_verification: Determine BlzRemoveEffect vs DestroyEffect semantics for current client before considering substitution
Retain synchronized creation/destruction ordering
Test effect attachment and animation behavior in DE/SD

native_api_candidate_inventory.use_case: Assess and generally reject as generalized renderer optimizers: terrain hiding and fog appearance controls are not safe automatic object culling
mandatory_verification: Do not claim fog is frustum culling
Do not hide terrain as an ordinary FPS solution

audit_workstreams.title: Map baseline and bottleneck separation
investigate: Identify active DE/SD mode, Rebirth overrides, installed client build and active DLL/graphics API
Classify GPU-bound vs main-thread/AI/script bottleneck vs loading/streaming spikes
Inventory FPS settings and existing optimization toggles

audit_workstreams.title: Doodad visibility and native 3.0 index-based control
investigate: Locate all DoodadRender code and integration even if source lives outside repository or WE GUI
Assess static doodad count/type distribution and high-cost draw/material/particle models
Prototype design only: one-time doodad registry by index, spatial partition, differential reveal/hide, hysteresis, index stability
Examine BlzSetSingleDoodadAnimation and show/hide tokens with minimal reproducible test map
Compare index-based operations to SetDoodadAnimationRect and existing system; check seasonal animation states

audit_workstreams.title: DestructibleHider differential tile updates
investigate: Derive exactly overlapping previous/next tile rectangles and minimal exited/entered strips
Handle large teleports, map edges, initial (-1) origin, repeated same cell, runtime register/unregister, dead trees, gates and dynamic destructables
Measure ShowDestructable calls/frame, actual toggles/frame, 95th/99th-percentile camera-pan frame time
Preserve public API, hashtable layout and save/load stability
Propose safe opt-in debug counters and a reversible patch

audit_workstreams.title: UnitHider4 scheduling and group-native efficiency
investigate: Measure periodic 0.10s work, 0.50s visible sweeps, reference cache size, hidden cell visitation and large reference sets
Identify each GroupAddGroup call whose semantics allow BlzGroupAddGroupFast and verify order/destroy flag
Check movement relocation hooks and whether hidden references or cinematic sweeps cause bursts
Keep current event-driven v4.11.0 structure and ownership model
Distinguish rendered-unit savings from AI/order/pathfinding savings

audit_workstreams.title: DynamicFarZ/camera/unified visibility distances
investigate: Measure frame cost for FarZ/zoom/pitch across Light/Medium/Heavy and specific camera contexts
Design optional profile hard-caps at the horizon and optional distance coordination with unit/doodad/destructable culling
Analyze local camera frequency, redundant SetCameraField calls and threshold/hysteresis methods
Preserve all free camera, developer mode, cutscene and special-area visibility authoring

audit_workstreams.title: Special effects and projectile/particle lifecycles
investigate: Inventory AddSpecialEffect*/DestroyEffect counts, update loops, persistent effects, dummy units and expensive particle models
Identify opportunities for combined transform natives and deferred updates
Test LOD/visibility/particle simplification for off-screen decorative effects without touching combat semantics
Investigate effects whose visible complexity is disproportionately expensive in DE
Do not assume effect pooling or invisible alpha necessarily saves draw calls

audit_workstreams.title: Weather visual budget
investigate: Measure rain-impact ring buffer, terrain sampling and precipitation during actual storms
Measure snow unit waves and steam attachments by zone
Check current FPS toggles, local camera anchoring and effect creation/destruction symmetry across clients
Define optional weather-budget profiles with same narrative intensity and stable gameplay

audit_workstreams.title: AI, ambient entities, movement and pathfinding
investigate: Detect expensive pathfinding/order storms with many off-screen units
Investigate AI tick batching, state-aware update rates and movement order deduplication
Design a SEPARATE simulation-LOD policy for NPCs only where gameplay semantics permit
Protect live combat, quest triggers, patrols requiring progression, persistent state and independent AI heroes
Benchmark CPU main-thread improvement in DE and SD

audit_workstreams.title: UI, dynamic minimap and text updates
investigate: Inventory frequent frame text/texture updates, inactive/hidden UI loops, minimap updates and 0.03125s floating text updates
Check BlzFrameSetVisible and update gating, caching of formatted strings and camera distance checks
Design visibility-driven execution gates without changing UX, tooltip or input behavior

audit_workstreams.title: Native/BJ wrapper and allocation audit across active sources
files: all active JASS/vJASS excluding generated/history unless imported
investigate: Search high-frequency GetUnitsInRectMatching/GetUnitsInRangeOfLocMatching calls allocating groups; GroupAddGroup/GroupRemoveGroup loops
Search repeated Location/GetUnitLoc/GetDestructableLoc/GetRandomLocInRect and repeated DestroyBoolExpr allocation
Search repeat timers, period <=0.10s, WorldBounds scans and nested enumerations

audit_workstreams.title: Graphics asset complexity / Rebirth / DE-specific rendering
files: World Editor object and doodad data (read-only)

audit_workstreams.title: Historical reports and regression hazards
investigate: Mark historical references to UnitHider3 and periodic UnitStats as stale where current code differs
Assess save/load from older map revisions, cached handle/group rebuild and index stability
Check deindex/revive/remove/cinematics/quests/destructable resurrection and World Editor backups
Create per-change rollback and validation gates

measurement_protocol.instrumentation_preference: Use external capture (PresentMon/CapFrameX or comparable) for FPS, frametime and 1% lows. Add optional JASS debug instrumentation only in a separately authorized experiment; the current audit is read-only.
controlled_variables: Exact map build and game build
same camera location, pitch and FarZ
same resolution, renderer (DX11/DX12), V-Sync state and graphics settings
same hardware, drivers and run duration
scenes: ambient NPC area with many moving units
metrics: frame-time spikes during camera tile crossings
GPU utilization and GPU frame time where available
CPU main-thread utilization / frame time where available
active units, visible units, hidden units, doodads, destructables, effects
per-tick toggles, effect creation/destruction, expensive group operation counts
measurement_protocol.ab_test_policy: One isolated reversible candidate at a time. Repeat trials and compare frame-time distributions. Report hardware/settings/measurement noise. Do not infer significance from single runs.
measurement_protocol.priority_formula: Rank by expected measurable impact x confidence x implementation safety, adjusted downward for regression risk and maintenance cost; disclose the chosen scoring rubric.
measurement_protocol.test_capabilities: If the Codex environment cannot launch game or record frametimes, provide a reproducible human-run test matrix and report results as NOT_MEASURED.

regression_matrix: Regular SD graphics and Warcraft III DE/HD graphics
Singleplayer map, multiplayer-safe synchronized execution and per-player local camera
Save/load and map version changes; never rely on volatile doodad indexes in saved user data without proof
UnitHider enable/disable, fresh map bootstrap, move/teleport, cinematic begin/end and refresh
Quest NPCs, vendors, companions, tamed units, neutral units and AI hero revealers
Destructable harvest, death, resurrection, bridges/gates, collision/pathing and dynamic registration
Terrain/world visibility, sky, water, fog and scripted camera angles
UI frame focus, minimap, tooltip, inventory, settings panels and mouse orbit
Continuous gameplay for 30+ minutes, forced teleport/reveal/hide cycles and load-state recovery

expected_codex_deliverables.path_suggestion: _developer/PerformanceAudit/ (create only with user permission; otherwise return report contents in chat)
expected_codex_deliverables.response_in_chat: Summarize five highest-priority code-evidenced findings, list the strongest 3.0-native opportunities, identify any missing/externally managed source, and name the first 3 isolated experiments. Do not claim completion of runtime tests that were not executed.

completion_gates: All cited code matches actual dev branch current files, not search-index main or obsolete reports.
Each native optimization identifies whether the gain is JASS/CPU work reduction, draw-call/GPU work reduction, simulation reduction, allocation reduction or merely a visual-quality tradeoff.
Each higher-priority recommendation supplies a minimal backwards-compatible patch design without editing it yet.
No proposal modifies simulation or local/synchronized behavior without an explicit safety argument.
All unclear APIs, especially per-index doodad 'show'/'hide', have an executable micro-test design.
The plan includes baseline and A/B benchmark protocol, observable thresholds, rollout order and rollback path.
Any repository-generated artifact complies with AGENTS.md and World Editor export constraints.
